## RD-04 — Shared JSON diagnostics contract

**Disposition:** TEST CHANGE. **Status:** pending independent Test Reviewer review.
**Assignment:** owner's unified downstream handoff; Architect Reviewer **OK, no
findings**, for registration `37e68764202a2a18e0c54ac264df1536ff47e28c`, verified
as the direct successor of `8ef05dff0d5bc942b7b5f35a3545a5efff56676f`. This is a
same-target F1 correction of `021961b767e3bc461708c86671b0f7fbc0a9c5fd`, reviewed
**NOT OK**. No procedural waiver or prior-review reuse applies.
The owner authorizes independent downstream work after architectural OK without
another downstream sign-off. The previously accepted RD-02 test assignment is closed.

**Accepted basis:** DK-DIAG-04's shared report contract and its DK-DIAG-05/§15
qualifications. The report, diagnostic entries and source-location entries are JSON
objects. Required members are: report `outcome` and `diagnostics`; diagnostic
`severity`, `code`, `message`, `effect`, `sources`, `generated_iri`; source location
`path`, `identifier`, `element_type`. The accepted enum/string/array/object/null
representations and required presence are asserted directly. Empty diagnostics
and source context use arrays, not omitted keys. Additional members are permitted;
consumers ignore them. No schema_version, fixed message, key order, event order or
condition-to-code catalogue is imposed. Only the former unspecified JSON structure
and member-name qualifications are superseded; Python API representations remain
implementation choices. Diagnostic production, consolidation, content restrictions,
console filtering, outcomes, abort/output eligibility and delivery failures retain
their meaning. No new normative behavior is introduced by test wiring.

**Initialization and source evidence:** both governing specifications were read
fully at role initialization. The complete RD-04 registration delta and affected
current diagnostic/API clauses were subsequently retrieved and checked; structure
blob `250a059d46377360aeecdb5176310bd36bde7825` is unchanged. Current transformation
blob is `07c3b20ae236500efd9bf59299c6e31f249fbcd0`. Correction base/main at
inspection is `6962d68f972466e7b8d5445cfe1e72cca4a0c282`. DK-DIAG-04, DK-DIAG-05
and §15 are unchanged from the RD-04 registration. Available public conversion/result/CLI interfaces,
actual producer fields, existing pytest assertions, support and inventory were
inspected independently. Production determines binding only, not expected fields.

**Initial publication reconciliation:** before publication, main advanced to
`c9bd97c970ef6789c0edb35cf0cac757ba3c5c51`. The intervening commit changes six
root/site-documentation files only. Its changes are incorporated; every test,
fixture, production and governing-specification blob remains unchanged. Source
and scope comparison, not repeated production execution, verifies that this
documentation-only advance does not affect the recorded runs.

**Fixture contracts:** reuse only `shared/base_iri/input.json` and
`shared/instantiation/input.json` under `tests/fixtures/`. Each node selects its
exact complete source, with explicit runtime mutations written to pytest temporary
files. Stored sources and Turtle/YAML companions are unchanged. There is no new
fixture bundle, source builder framework or structural exception. Malformed JSON,
null source IDs, duplicate declarations, a missing metadata.yaml and an unrecognized
null-typed element are deliberate governed negatives, not new supported shapes.
Recognized-class flags set to null use their accepted no-explicit-Boolean behavior.
The missing metadata path has the required metadata.yaml basename and no file is
invented or automatically discovered.

The existing VP-plugin 0.5.3 provenance remains applicable. One Catalog source was
reinspected: `models/library/ontology.json` at Catalog revision
`99d23ff1e1c2bf58a7bd99ef0156eba79a611c99`, blob
`0ef9f0b0543eb31035489907160d9759c6166d45`. Its Project/Package/Class structure
and nullable fields corroborate the canonical fixtures. It declares no exporter
version; no claim that it is a certified 0.5.3 export is made. No raw Catalog model
is copied or processed by the suite and no Catalog-wide audit is performed.

**Actual invocation evidence:** the replaceable adapter calls the real public
ConversionResult.export_diagnostics and adapts its native success or actual
DiagnosticsExportError, retaining the original exception. Python's existing reader/
report-writer profile observes whether conversion automatically exports diagnostics;
it now applies to ordinary calls as well as version-IRI calls. It does not infer
absence from an option or create reports to satisfy an expectation.

For CLI completeness, the existing same-process profile independently copies the
native result immediately on conversion return and after CLI delivery. Both
snapshots precede interpretation of the test's JSON observations; neither is read
from a report or generated by export_report/asdict. Tests require preservation of
conversion-time events and compare the final native events to the raw JSON, with
multiplicity retained and ordering ignored. Console severity counts are read from
captured bytes and checked against the selected threshold. This remains valid with
INFO/WARNING hidden from the console; filtered presentation is never evidence that
no event was produced. The extra snapshot data is test-side instrumentation, not a
production API requirement. Missing observation evidence remains explicitly unbound.

The JSON reader retains complete raw files while interpreting only known members;
extra members at report/diagnostic/source levels are ignored compatibly. Existing
PLACEHOLDER_BASE, DERIVED_STATUS_ANNOTATION and
DISCARDED_INSTANTIATION_INFORMATION values are interpreted only as inspected
implementation binding knowledge, not as registered normative identifiers. Placeholder
facts are read from actual wording. Code/message/effect values in assertions come
from actual native events, never fixed expected literals. The existing CLI
instantiation row below is corrected to reject exact discarded source values,
rather than a prefix also occurring in a legitimate diagnostic code; its node,
consolidation check and other assertions are preserved.

**Branches:** ten Python export scenarios and the same ten CLI scenarios at all
three console levels cover clean output, INFO, generated-IRI WARNING, a global
WARNING without sources, recoverable ERROR, malformed-source abort, metadata-file
abort, unavailable element type, WARNING followed by duplicate-ID abort, and
instantiation consolidation/value restrictions. Three real Python export failures
preserve native diagnostics, graph eligibility and outcome. No fake conversion,
blanket skip/xfail or production fault hook is introduced.

The compatibility-reader case is **harness only**: a real exported file is augmented
with permitted members and reordered, then consumed by the adapter. It receives no
DirectKG transformation credit. All other new rows exercise real conversion and/or
public export behavior. Expected field/type assertions remain in the owning tests;
the invocation layer never supplies expected output.

**Initial submission validation:** Python 3.12.14, pytest 9.1.1, RDFLib 7.6.0 and PyYAML 6.0.3.
Collection is **3,308**, retaining all **3,264** prior nodes. There are **43 new
behavioral cases plus one reader/harness case**, all **44 passed**, with no skips,
xfails, assertion failures or collection errors in that selection. Current inventory
contains **3,219 behavioral nodes**; 89 fixture/helper/reader nodes receive no
transformation coverage credit.

The same **526 pre-existing input-diagnostics/CLI nodes** change from **371 passed /
155 unbound failures** at the publication baseline to **385 passed / 141 existing
unbound failures**. No previous pass regresses and no old node disappears. Remaining
failures are all ImplementationUnavailable: 92 operations, 16 console-kind reads,
eight prohibited-feature reads, seven provenance-role reads, fourteen broader
control inspections and four other unbound provenance/configuration/stdout readers.
Unavailable fault, serialization, delivery and broader interpretation capabilities
are not credited as passing. This is a scoped adapter extension, not a full binding.

Additional affected adapter regressions: **176 passed**, including the accepted
RD-02 membership nodes, opaque identities and generic fallback behavior. All **88
existing fixture/RDF-helper checks** pass. Both JSON checkers independently reject
27 required-member/type/container/enum faults and detect seven mirroring faults;
they each accept four permitted extension/null/opaque-code/ordering variants. These
scratch controls use actual produced reports and do not earn transformation credit.
Two further real-CLI controls truncate only the final test-observation snapshot;
both reject lost hidden diagnostics using the independent conversion-return copy.
All 17 test/support and 21 production Python files parse; production files are read
only. Inventory/rule/path consistency and git diff --check pass.

Actual commands (repository root; isolated Python environment, XML/log destinations
outside the repository):

```bash
python -m pytest --rootdir=. --collect-only -q tests
python -m pytest --rootdir=. -q tests/transformation/test_input_diagnostics.py tests/cli/test_cli.py -k shared_json_contract --tb=short -rN
python -m pytest --rootdir=. -q tests/transformation/test_input_diagnostics.py tests/cli/test_cli.py -k 'not shared_json_contract' --tb=no -rN
python -m pytest --rootdir=. -q tests/transformation/test_classes.py tests/transformation/test_higher_order.py tests/transformation/test_relations.py tests/transformation/test_iris.py -k 'repeated_membership or opaque_identifiers or generic_fallback' --tb=no -rN
python -m pytest --rootdir=. -q tests -k 'fixture_contract or rdf_helper' --tb=short -rN
```

The baseline was independently rerun from a detached worktree at
`37e68764202a2a18e0c54ac264df1536ff47e28c` with its source directory on PYTHONPATH,
not by reverting the active work. Full-suite execution, full provenance conformance,
external deployment and unbound operations remain unperformed. Published test
artifacts require independent Test Reviewer review and do not certify whole-project
production correctness.

**F1 correction and validation (2026-11-07):** the reviewer found that the two
Python export functions inspected `result.ontology`, a conversion-time observation,
after export operated on the live result. Both now call the already-bound
`invoke.read_ontology(result)` after the real export attempt. Non-aborted graphs
must remain present and isomorphic to their independent pre-export copies; aborted
results must remain without a graph. Existing Rules, fixtures, IDs and the other
31 RD-04 cases are preserved. This repairs test observation under DK-DIAG-04's
non-interference and diagnostics-delivery-failure clauses, DK-DIAG-05's output
eligibility and §15; it adds no normative behavior or production API requirement.

Reproduced F1 using `clean`, `partial` and `duplicate_abort` in each affected
function. Each control invokes real conversion and a real successful/failed export,
then replaces only `result.native.ontology`: eligible graphs become absent and
aborted results acquire a graph. All six controls falsely passed before correction;
all six now fail at the live graph's presence/absence assertions. These scratch
controls are validation evidence, not additional pytest or transformation coverage.

Fresh execution with the same declared Python/dependency versions: all **44 RD-04
cases pass**, including the 13 corrected cases. The **nine directly affected
pre-existing diagnostic-access/export cases** yield **8 passed, 1 failed**; the
failure is the existing unbound required-provenance construction fault
(`ImplementationUnavailable`), before export. No production defect is inferred.
Full collection remains **3,308**, retaining all prior exact nodes. Inventory
node/rule/path consistency, parsing of all 17 test/support and 21 production Python
files, and git diff --check pass. Earlier broad regressions, fixture checks and
shape/mirroring controls above were not rerun for this two-function correction.
Full-suite execution, full provenance conformance and unbound operations remain
unperformed. No skip/xfail is introduced.

Correction commands (repository root; `python` is the isolated Python 3.12.14
executable). The first scratch command ran before editing; the second ran after:

```bash
python /workspace/scratch/e3629d4acf8b/rd04-f1-validation/graph_replacement_controls.py --expect escaped
python /workspace/scratch/e3629d4acf8b/rd04-f1-validation/graph_replacement_controls.py --expect rejected
python -m pytest --rootdir=. -q tests/transformation/test_input_diagnostics.py tests/cli/test_cli.py -k shared_json_contract --tb=short -rN
python -m pytest --rootdir=. -q tests/transformation/test_input_diagnostics.py -k 'programmatic_diagnostic_access_is_complete_and_noninterfering or python_diagnostics_export_is_explicit_complete_and_noninterfering_even_after_abort' --tb=short -rN
python -m pytest --rootdir=. --collect-only -q tests
git diff --check
```

`07c3b20ae236500efd9bf59299c6e31f249fbcd0` and organizational structure blob
`250a059d46377360aeecdb5176310bd36bde7825` remain current. The owner authorizes

confirmation; this overrides older sequencing references only. No review reuse
or additional procedural waiver applies. The RD-04 F1 test gate at
`d74c0e7da378d88abbf5c400d2e7b3d6488dc35a` is closed by owner-relayed independent OK.

**Accepted clauses and supersession:** DK-REL-01 retains ordinary identity,
direction, naming, labels, descriptions, domain/range, cardinalities, inverses,
generalizations and independently required source annotations for all three
stereotypes. No additional logical axioms or declaration annotations are generated
solely from them. DK-GEN-11's metadata permission does not override that omission.
DK-REL-04 and DK-DIAG-01 preserve the applicable limitation WARNING despite naming
success; it is nonfatal under strict, tolerant and best-effort. Naming precedence,
controls, language, diagnostic content/consolidation/filtering/reporting, and
independent errors/abort policies remain applicable. No native diagnostic code,
message template or count is fixed. No accepted mapping is superseded: only the
previously unresolved status of these three treatments is replaced. The earlier
five RD-17 additions, `participational` asymmetry and per-axiom compatibility gate
are unchanged; other open groups are outside this assignment.

**Assessment and smallest sufficient change:** existing six stereotype-table
nodes asserted exact successful lexical candidates, primary direction and absence
of naming errors, but no limitation warning. They now also assert the independently
required WARNING, retaining their exact IDs and candidates. Existing generic
ordinary/cardinality/inverse tests and the historical-dependence absence audit did
not assert this decision for these three stereotypes. Add 39 cases in the approved
relations module: nine ordinary-mapping/profile cases, 24 naming/control cases
(each exercises both represented directions), and six explicit-hierarchy cases.
Three existing helper bodies are unchanged while their names and every consumer
are generalized for shared relation use. No parallel suite or unused scaffold.

**Fixtures and supported input:** reuse canonical `shared/binary_relation` and
`relations/hierarchy`, with complete VP-plugin 0.5.3-style Project/Package/Class/
Relation/Property/Generalization records and bounded Project.languages enrichment.
Each runtime document is checked by fixture_issues before actual conversion,
including the ordinary control and both represented naming directions. No stored
input/expected graph, fixture move, dependency or pytest configuration changes.
Mutations supply a kind/event pair, fixed names, source descriptions (including
stereotype text), finite end counts, independent read-only/ordered/begin/end flags,
and supported controls. Hierarchy changes only the leaf's relation stereotype.
There are no new malformed-input cases or inferred exporter version claims.

`degraded_entity` to `process`. Its ordered binary properties and reference shapes
match the authoring contract; it declares no exporter version. Existing canonical
fixtures are adapted in place at runtime, not extracted from that raw model:
short stable IDs/names and a kind/event pair isolate accepted mappings; reverse
cases exchange only endpoint references. Complete hierarchy fixtures supply the
separately governed generalization structure. Catalog names/examples determine
no expected behavior, and no whole-Catalog processing or provenance certification
is claimed.

Official VP-plugin 0.5.3 source at `9fc02b8162db9910f21b8713549cafce2627dad0`
was inspected: RelationStereotype.java recognizes all three; IAssociationTransformer.java
preserves ordered ends; RelationSerializer.java, ClassifierSerializer.java and
PropertySerializer.java establish the fields/null/reference forms used. Paths are
under `src/main/java/it/unibz/inf/ontouml/vp/model/` in
https://github.com/OntoUML/ontouml-vp-plugin . Catalog source:
https://github.com/OntoUML/ontouml-models/blob/99d23ff1e1c2bf58a7bd99ef0156eba79a611c99/models/garcia2022human-genome-events/ontology.json .

**Invocation and absence evidence:** real public conversion/result RDF and native
diagnostics remain bound through tests/support/invocation.py. The new scoped
read_relation_stereotype_annotations method delegates to the existing inspected
actual-RDF audit: source-authored descriptions/names, known independent flag and
begin/end forms, permitted timestamps and recognized logical forms are audited;
unrecognized annotation/predicate/auxiliary forms raise ImplementationUnavailable.
No empty observation is supplied from requested options or expected fixtures.
Positive declaration forms remain unbound until inspectable. Direct RDF assertions
check property labels/IDs; paired ordinary controls and logical graph projections
compare classes, incoming domain/range subjects, restrictions, lists and logical
resources by isomorphism, allowing independent metadata. Fixed source/naming/count
assertions anchor those controls. The native existing diagnostic renderer is
binding knowledge only, not a prescribed code catalogue. No fake warning, test
transformer, skip or xfail is used. CLI/report policy remains under its existing
acceptance cases and is not replaced here.

**Execution:** Python 3.12.14, pytest 9.1.1, RDFLib 7.6.0, PyYAML 6.0.3.
Full collection is **3,347**, retaining all **3,308** prior exact nodes; 39 are
added and none renamed/removed. The combined affected selection executes 172:
**127 passed, 45 failed**. Every failure is the final required limitation-warning
assertion: 39 new nodes plus the six intentionally strengthened prior nodes.
Earlier output/mapping/naming/annotation assertions pass. Both naming directions
run before checking the warning. No unexpected assertion, production exception,
binding failure or fixture failure occurs. The missing WARNING is a production
omission exposed by valid test-first assertions, not a passing test result.

Baseline selections before edits: **100 passed** for existing names/historical/
core additions; **90 passed** for the previous five-axiom selection. Their union
is 133 exact prior nodes. All 127 unchanged selected nodes retain their passes;
the other six acquire only this decision's warning assertion. The 90-case
five-axiom selection remains passing, including both `participational` directions
and its non-simple/simplicity gate cases. All **88 existing fixture/RDF-helper
checks pass**. Unknown annotation forms are unbound in deliberate scratch controls,
not failures in the affected pytest execution.

Scratch controls over actual converted RDF reject 21 logical mutations across
the three stereotypes: characteristics, an incoming untyped foreign property,
restrictions, an ordered chain, a new logical class and property equivalence.
Twelve unfamiliar declaration/annotation/auxiliary forms raise explicit unavailability
rather than earning absence. Three timestamp variants and three actual source
texts naming the stereotype are accepted. No positive diagnostic is fabricated;
these controls receive no transformation coverage credit. All 17 test/support
and 21 production Python files parse, affected fixture authoring checks and
inventory/node/rule/path reconciliation pass, and git diff --check passes.
Full-suite execution, full provenance conformance, Catalog-wide validation and
broader unbound operations are unperformed. This submission awaits independent
Test Reviewer review; test acceptance would not certify production correctness.

## RD-17 — participational and manifestation, alternative A

**Disposition:** TEST CHANGE. **Status:** pending independent Test Reviewer review.
**Assignment and stage authority:** owner's unified handoff, acceptance “I accept
Alternative A with all five proposed boundaries”, and Architect Reviewer **OK,
no findings**, for exact registration `fb05478031e290b123e766ad5188e4cef9935357`.
Verified as current inspected main and the direct successor of publication base
`f125a0d20321cf6cfc1c74253e2b940d69fcd8d2`. The two active governing documents
remain transformation-specification.md (blob
`54510d68a663643db75d7bb4ea8e30329e06c074`) and test-suite-structure.md (unchanged
blob `250a059d46377360aeecdb5176310bd36bde7825`). Both were read fully at role
initialization; this assignment refreshes the full accepted delta, applicable
clauses, history, tests, fixtures, support and available public interfaces.
The owner permits independent downstream work; another engineer's work, review,
sign-off or no-action confirmation is not a prerequisite. This overrides older
sequencing references only; independent Test Reviewer review remains required.
No correction, prior-review reuse or additional procedural waiver applies.
The preceding three-stereotype test gate at
`363d0d37bb1ae56a0ef3cdc762dd3ca7d4994dc6` is closed by owner-relayed independent OK.

**Accepted five boundaries:** DK-REL-01 retains ordinary property identity,
direction, naming, labels, descriptions, domains/ranges, explicit counts,
inverses, generalizations and independently required annotations/axioms for both
stereotypes. Retain participational asymmetry and its existing compatibility gate;
manifestation contributes no new property characteristic. Generate no further
stereotype-only logical axioms or declaration annotations. Require a nonfatal
residual-semantics WARNING for each successfully mapped eligible relation under
strict, tolerant and best-effort, independently of naming success or emitted/
gate-omitted asymmetry. Preserve diagnostic consolidation/content/delivery and
independent errors/abort rules; no exact code, wording or count is prescribed.
Document partial translation and remove only these two unresolved questions.
DK-GEN-11, DK-REL-04 and DK-DIAG-01 align that boundary. No accepted mapping is
superseded, and the earlier five additions/compatibility gate and remaining groups
are unchanged. No temporal subsystem, event-parthood vocabulary extension,
semantic validation, repair or global OWL-profile guarantee is inferred.

**Applicability and smallest sufficient change:** existing stereotype naming and
gate assertions cover accepted mappings but lack this pair's required warning.
Extend the current partial-relation functions with 26 parameters: six ordinary
profiles, sixteen naming/control cases (both directions in each), and four
hierarchy cases. Add nine mode/policy gate cases using shared existing gate
assertions. Strengthen 18 exact existing nodes: four semantic naming cells,
eleven participational whole-marker cases, and three insufficient-role policy
cells. All previous IDs and expectations remain; only these warning assertions
are added. Existing gate assertions move intact into a shared helper, retaining
all original test nodes and default options. No parallel suite or new fixture
framework. The existing annotation-reader body is unchanged; its description
now includes all settled partial-relation stereotypes.

**Input/fixture contracts and adaptations:** reuse complete canonical
shared/binary_relation, relations/hierarchy and relations/chain_constraints JSON.
Every runtime input is checked by fixture_issues before conversion, including
paired ordinary controls. There is no stored JSON/Turtle/YAML or fixture move,
new dependency/configuration, or production API requirement. Bounded
Project.languages enrichment and language overrides retain their existing rules.
There are no new malformed-input cases; existing absent/null/zero/two-marker
variants retain their accepted treatment and gain only the independent warning.

Selected Catalog files at `99d23ff1e1c2bf58a7bd99ef0156eba79a611c99` were parsed:

- `models/garcia2022human-genome-events/ontology.json`, blob
  `0e2006d52d521be3ad2994941aec969ef38ac65c`: participational relation
  `DJwh6r6EifjQiREu` links participation_in_biological_event to process, both
  event classes; source count 1..*, target count 1, target COMPOSITE marker.
- `models/guizzardi2022ufo/ontology.json`, blob
  `900c8d34f4bc9252832c257cfc0733a222dc268b`: manifestation relation
  `j7Yr.V6GAqACDCIB` links Jog (mode) to Jogging Event (event), with source count
  1 and target count 1..*.

Both use ordered binary properties and typed ID references, declare no exporter
version, and are inspected evidence rather than copied complete suite fixtures.
Runtime adaptations retain the source type patterns with short stable IDs and
PartEvent/WholeEvent or Aspect/Event names. Reversal exchanges endpoint references;
participational whole markers move with the same whole-event occurrence. Both
SHARED and COMPOSITE and ambiguous/missing markers retain their accepted existing
matrix assertions. Counts/flags/language are controlled to isolate accepted
mappings, without importing Catalog semantics as requirements. Hierarchy and
chain fixtures provide separately accepted structures. No whole-Catalog processing,
frequency claim, exporter-provenance certification or end-to-end Catalog conformance
is made. Sources:
https://github.com/OntoUML/ontouml-models/blob/99d23ff1e1c2bf58a7bd99ef0156eba79a611c99/models/garcia2022human-genome-events/ontology.json
https://github.com/OntoUML/ontouml-models/blob/99d23ff1e1c2bf58a7bd99ef0156eba79a611c99/models/guizzardi2022ufo/ontology.json

Official VP-plugin 0.5.3 source at `9fc02b8162db9910f21b8713549cafce2627dad0`
was inspected again: RelationStereotype.java recognizes both stereotypes;
IAssociationTransformer.java preserves ordered ends; RelationSerializer.java,
ClassifierSerializer.java and PropertySerializer.java confirm the fields and
nullable/reference shapes used. Paths are under
`src/main/java/it/unibz/inf/ontouml/vp/model/` in
https://github.com/OntoUML/ontouml-vp-plugin . No newer standalone schema is imposed.

**Assertions and invocation:** real public file conversion, eligible RDF graphs
and raw native diagnostics remain bound through the unchanged invocation behavior.
The annotation reader audits actual triples/source text and known independent
forms; unknown annotations/predicates/auxiliaries raise explicit unavailability.
No options or expected fixtures stand in for evidence. The logical comparison
now accepts explicit fixed expected additions on a copied ordinary expectation:
only the already accepted primary participational asymmetry for controlled simple
fixtures or the gate's mode-none case. Actual/ordinary result graphs are not
mutated; no conversion is simulated. Manifestation and gate-omitted asymmetry
admit no added characteristic. Fixed identity, direction, naming, counts, labels,
IDs/omission and independent comments anchor the comparisons; graph equality is
by isomorphism, without Turtle order, blank-node names or unrequired entailments.
No positive warning is fabricated. The semantic warning kind is test-side binding
knowledge, not a selected diagnostic identifier. Existing consolidation and
reporting requirements remain intact; no new count or renderer literal is imposed.

**Actual validation:** Python 3.12.14, pytest 9.1.1, RDFLib 7.6.0, PyYAML 6.0.3.
Full collection is **3,382**, retaining all **3,347** previous exact nodes and
adding 35. The final combined selection executes 269: **216 passed, 53 failed**.
All failures reach the required residual WARNING assertion: 35 new nodes and
18 deliberately strengthened nodes. Earlier output, annotation, naming and gate
assertions pass, including both represented naming directions and every gate/
policy branch before warning checks. No fixture/binding failure, unexpected
assertion, error, skip or xfail occurs. These are valid test-first failures for
missing production warning coverage, not passing implementation evidence.

The identical pre-existing selection at the pinned publication baseline executes
**234 passed**. All 216 unchanged selected nodes retain passes; the remaining 18
receive only this accepted warning requirement. The existing 90-case five-addition
compatibility subset passes within the combined execution. All **88 fixture/
RDF-helper checks pass**. Collection, Rules, exact IDs, fixture/expectation paths,
all 17 test/support and 21 production Python parses, and whitespace checks pass.

Scratch controls over actual graphs accept the two ordinary-to-stereotyped
comparisons and authored stereotype text; fourteen added logical mutations fail,
and removal of the required participational asymmetry also fails. Eight unknown
annotation forms raise explicit unavailability instead of assumed absence.
Two blank-node relabelings and two permitted timestamp variants are accepted.
These controls get no transformation-coverage credit and create no positive
warning or replacement conversion. Full-suite execution, full provenance
conformance, Catalog-wide processing, positive declaration interpretation and
broader unbound operations remain unperformed. No essential normative branch is
blocked in this submission.

Actual commands (repository root; declared isolated Python environment; XML/logs
outside the repository):

```bash
python -m pytest --rootdir=. --collect-only -q tests
python -m pytest --rootdir=. -q tests/transformation/test_relations.py -k '(partial_semantic_relations and (participational or manifestation)) or participational_limitation_warning' --tb=short -rN
python -m pytest --rootdir=. -q tests/transformation/test_relations.py -k 'partial_semantic_relations or participational_limitation_warning or stereotype_table_candidates or historical_dependence_ or additional_relation_characteristics or feature_disjointness or feature_pairing or chain_body_participation or new_relation_axioms or imported_non_simple or aggregation_flags_preserve or unique_whole_marker or insufficient_structural_roles' --tb=short -rN
python -m pytest --rootdir=. -q tests -k 'fixture_contract or rdf_helper' --tb=short -rN
python /workspace/scratch/e3629d4acf8b/rd17-pair-validation/output_controls.py
git diff --check
```

The baseline is a detached worktree at
`fb05478031e290b123e766ad5188e4cef9935357`, with its source pinned on PYTHONPATH.
Its regression command is the combined selection above without the new
participational_limitation_warning selector; the added partial-relation parameters
are absent from that revision. Initial smaller runs (172 baseline passes;
168 passes/39 missing warnings before adding existing marker-policy checks) are
intermediate evidence only; the final counts above govern this submission.
Production, governing documents, vocabulary and site documentation are read only.
Status remains pending independent Test Reviewer disposition.

## RD-17 — Dependency relations and warning consistency

**Disposition** TEST CHANGE. **Status** F1–F3 correction pending independent Test
Reviewer review. The initial submission at
`545d995b68fd4f97ca7c0c2183ea02fd53328328` received **NOT OK** for warning
attribution, naming-bypass coverage, and class-disjointness comparison.
**Authority:** owner-forwarded unified handoff and Architect Reviewer **OK, no
findings**, for exact registration `490f209e0d70533bac56674e2844a7463fe77a09`.
Owner acceptance: “I accept Alternative A with all five proposed boundaries.”
The simultaneous owner direction removes case-by-case approval for analogous
residual warnings, preserving independent review and explicit exceptions. The
registration applies it to bringsAbout/triggers warnings only. It does not give
the Test Engineer authority to resolve their remaining graph questions.

The original assessment inspected the registration, which directly follows
`98481308e0e3592e369e2d1b9241f1afecf83497`. The reviewed behavioral source is
transformation-specification.md, blob `6492a064d62ee6c742dd4a27b0f83e6bf0adb92b`.
The placement source is test-suite-structure.md, blob
`250a059d46377360aeecdb5176310bd36bde7825`. Both governing documents were read
fully at role initialization; this assessment refreshes the complete accepted
delta, affected rules, history, tests, fixtures, inventory, support and available
public production interfaces. Independent downstream work follows the owner's
explicit instruction without another engineer's work/review/sign-off/no-action
confirmation as a prerequisite. Independent Test Reviewer review remains required.
No prior-review reuse or additional waiver applies. The preceding pair's test
gate at `00f9bf1503b271da1c84728d0ce511efaf505483` is closed by owner-relayed OK.

**Accepted five boundaries and qualifications:** DK-REL-01 preserves mediation,
characterization and externalDependence ordinary identity, direction, names,
labels, descriptions, domains/ranges, explicit counts, inverses, generalizations
and independent annotations. Retain accepted characteristics, paired disjointness,
compatibility gates, grounding roles, derivation and optional chains unchanged.
No further stereotype-only logical axioms/declaration annotations are introduced
for the trio. Successfully mapped eligible ordinary relations require a nonfatal
residual WARNING under strict/tolerant/best-effort, despite naming, accepted-axiom/
chain generation or gate-based omission. Existing diagnostic exceptions, content,
consolidation and delivery remain applicable; no exact code, wording or count is
selected. Partial translation does not mean applicable mappings were discarded.

DK-GEN-11, DK-REL-04 and DK-DIAG-01 align that treatment. At the reviewed
registration, the same nonfatal warning rule applies to bringsAbout/triggers
and settles their warning component. The subsequent registration on the
publication base settles their graph treatment separately. This correction
exercises the original mapping and warning requirements for the pair.

**Applicability and change.** The initial 90 additions include 39 trio
mapping/naming/hierarchy cases, 27 gate cases, 18 grounding/chain cases and six
warning-only event/situation cases. The 13 strengthened nodes include ten
successful semantic-name cases and three external-dependence insufficient-role
cases. Previous IDs, lexical expectations and original
chain/gate assertions remain. Original chain assertions are shared intact through
a helper with the same default options. Existing gate helper and applicable
constraint/disjointness policies remain unchanged. The F1–F3 correction retains
every reviewed ID and adds two `strict` naming-disabled event/situation cases.
Both cases exercise the accepted endpoint fallback, its naming warning, and the
residual warning. The correction applies existing rules to test assertions.

**Fixtures and expected output:** canonical shared/binary_relation,
shared/material_pattern, relations/hierarchy and relations/chain_constraints
remain complete supported VP-plugin 0.5.3-style JSON. Every runtime variant is
checked by fixture_issues before real file conversion; both naming directions
have distinct temporary sources. There is no stored fixture/expectation, dependency,
configuration or structure change. Fixed source/naming/count/label/ID assertions
anchor paired ordinary comparisons. Those comparisons add only explicit accepted
primary asymmetry/irreflexivity to a copied expectation; no actual graph changes.
The comparison checks `owl:disjointWith` as unordered class pairs under
DK-CLS-03/04 and detects missing and added pairs.
Gate and chain cases retain ordered chains, compatible characteristics/aligned
pairs, explicit hierarchy, inverse forms and mode-specific constraints. Expected
RDF is compared by isomorphism or targeted asserted/absent triples, never byte
order, blank-node identity or unrequired entailments. Pair warning tests use only
existing positive mapping assertions and diagnostic checks, with no negative RDF
or declaration-annotation policy selected for them.

**Source evidence and adaptations:** selected Catalog files at
`99d23ff1e1c2bf58a7bd99ef0156eba79a611c99` were parsed independently:

- `models/guizzardi2022ufo/ontology.json`, blob
  `900c8d34f4bc9252832c257cfc0733a222dc268b`, contains 14 mediation, four
  characterization and three externalDependence relations. Examples include
  Employment mediating Teacher/School and the mode/feature patterns recorded in
  the accepted research history. These are selected-file counts only.
- `models/rodrigues2019ontocrime/ontology.json`, blob
  `29ff7625931f729d9d3a0ed7456e42a1d730b0d5`, contains 12 mediation relations.
  Some endpoint classes lack stereotypes; no claim of whole-model conformance
  or certified exporter provenance is inferred from those records.

Both have Project/Package records and ordered binary properties with typed ID
references, and neither declares an exporter version. Runtime canonical variants
use short IDs and controlled Relator/Endurant, Bearer/Feature and Mode/Endurant
pairs, explicit names/flags/counts/language, and independently accepted grounding/
hierarchy structures. This isolates registered behavior without making Catalog
examples normative or copying unsupported complete models. No additional Catalog
occurrence is claimed for bringsAbout/triggers, whose existing event/situation
cases follow the registered naming table and warning-only scope. No Catalog-wide
processing, frequency, provenance certification or end-to-end audit is claimed.
Sources:
https://github.com/OntoUML/ontouml-models/blob/99d23ff1e1c2bf58a7bd99ef0156eba79a611c99/models/guizzardi2022ufo/ontology.json
https://github.com/OntoUML/ontouml-models/blob/99d23ff1e1c2bf58a7bd99ef0156eba79a611c99/models/rodrigues2019ontocrime/ontology.json

Official VP-plugin 0.5.3 source at `9fc02b8162db9910f21b8713549cafce2627dad0`
was inspected: RelationStereotype.java recognizes all five; IAssociationTransformer.java
retains ordered ends; RelationSerializer.java, ClassifierSerializer.java and
PropertySerializer.java confirm field/null/reference shapes. Files are under
`src/main/java/it/unibz/inf/ontouml/vp/model/` in
https://github.com/OntoUML/ontouml-vp-plugin . No newer standalone schema is imposed.

**Invocation and warning attribution.** The bound
`read_relation_limitation_source_ids` reader resolves actual residual WARNING
locators against the supplied source document and retains affected relation IDs.
The gate checks require the specific target relation. The chain checks require
both `rLeft` and `rRight`, including the two distinct mediations. A consolidated
warning can identify both. Uninterpretable locators raise
`ImplementationUnavailable`. The RDF annotation audit retains its existing
binding for actual source text and independently required annotation forms.

**Actual execution.** Python 3.12.14, pytest 9.1.1, RDFLib 7.6.0 and PyYAML 6.0.3.
The reviewed revision collected **3,472** cases. The correction collects
**3,474**, retaining all reviewed IDs. The same affected selection changed
from **256 passed, 103 failed** to **256 passed, 105 failed**. At the correction,
**78** fail at residual WARNING presence and **27** at target-relation
attribution. The two added cases reach the residual WARNING assertion after
the endpoint fallback, inverse, direction, outcome, and naming-warning checks.
The current producer omits the five required residual warnings.

All **90** existing compatibility cases passed within the affected run.
Another **68** mapping/disjointness, **88** fixture/RDF-helper, and **4** CLI
parity cases passed. The same **12** derivation cases encountered the existing
unbound connector-output reader at both revisions.

Scratch controls over actual `participational` warnings reproduced F1.
Either single warning failed the corrected two-relation coverage check.
Separate warnings, reordered warnings, and a consolidated control using both
reported locators passed. Two uninterpretable locator controls remained
explicitly unbound. For F3, copies of real graphs showed that all three
reversed disjointness statements falsely failed at the reviewed revision.
The correction accepted all three reversed and all three reciprocal variants
and rejected three missing and three added pairs. These controls exercise the
test harness. Full-suite execution, full provenance conformance, and positive
end-to-end execution of the five new warnings remain unperformed.
